definition: A collision in which the total kinetic energy of the bodies is the same afterwards as before; momentum is also conserved if no resultant external force acts, and head-on the bodies separate at the same relative speed at which they approached.
A collision in which the total kinetic energy decreases, because some is transferred to other forms such as internal energy and sound; momentum is still conserved if no resultant external force acts.
An event in which internal forces, using stored energy, push the parts of a system apart: with no resultant external force the total momentum is conserved, and the total kinetic energy increases.
